answer: An agent enters high-value markets only after locking stake and passing unpredictable, cross-agent challenge rounds whose answers are checked against private task context. Coordinated fakes are exposed when their results conflict, and the deposit is slashed. A Sybil attacker must therefore finance many deposits, maintain each identity, and absorb repeated losses when one fails; multiplying names becomes more expensive than honest work. A voyage can trigger a ripple of challenges, while a sparrow-sized account still pays the same bond.
